Umma at 7 pm

A home cook opens the app at dinnertime. This page walks what happens today, screen by screen, from the latest build on main. Then it lists where the evening falls short and what notifications could add.

Build: main @ 05f225fScreens captured 13 Nov 2026, iPhone simulator, light modeTest AI provider, sample creators
6:58 pmOpen the app

Explore opens on For You

The app always opens on Explore → For You. Nothing on screen says it's dinnertime. The feed looks the same at 7 am as it does at 7 pm.

For You ranks every published recipe by:

  • how many of its ingredients are in your pantry
  • whether it's a cuisine you picked in onboarding
  • whether you follow the cook who posted it
  • a penalty if it clashes with your diet

Each card says why it's there: You have 8 of 9, Korean, From Mina Cho or New. A recipe with one of your allergens is moved to the bottom and labelled. It is never hidden.

With an empty pantry, as in this screenshot, a card reading See what you can make tonight sits above the feed, and the ranking falls back to your cuisines and the cooks you follow.

7:00 pmTell it what's in the kitchen

Pantry: speak it, scan it, or type it

The three buttons at the top of Pantry are: say what you have, take a photo of the shelf, or add an item by hand. Anything the app detects is a suggestion. It joins the pantry only after you confirm it, and each item shows how it got there and when you confirmed it.

Back on For You, the pantry now drives the order. The Can make now chip filters down to recipes you have every ingredient for.

7:02 pmOr start from people

Following tab and creator pages

Following lists recipes from cooks you follow, newest first. It doesn't use your pantry. Tapping by Mina Cho on any recipe opens her page, where you can follow or unfollow.

The creators in these screenshots are fictional sample accounts loaded for testing.

7:04 pmPick a recipe

Recipe page, then Pantry fit

The recipe page has two actions: Check my pantry and Start cooking. Pantry fit sorts every ingredient into Available, Uncertain (you have it, but no amount is recorded) and Missing, and its headline says how many are missing.

This is the moment the user decides. In this example the recipe is missing 4 ingredients, which is a lot to accept at 7 pm.

7:06 pmSwap what's missing

Swaps you approve one at a time

For each missing ingredient, the app suggests swaps. Each one comes with:

  • how much of it to use
  • what changes in flavour and texture
  • how confident the app is in the swap
  • any warnings

Nothing is applied until you tap Use this swap. A swap that contains one of your allergens is shown as blocked, and you can't pick it.

7:08 pmCook

Step by step, with timers and a coach

Steps change only when you tap Next. A step affected by a swap is marked Adapted. Food-safety warnings appear in the step itself. Timers count down to a fixed end time, so they stay correct after the app has been closed and reopened.

The coach answers typed questions. It refuses to judge doneness or safety from a description or a photo.

7:45 pmFinish

How did it go, and keep my changes

At the end you rate the cook: Cooked it, Partly or Didn't work. The finish screen lists your swaps. Save my changes keeps them for the next time you cook this recipe.

Where the evening falls short

Gaps found while tracing the journey above against the code.

  • Nothing invites you back at 7 pmThe app sends no notifications of any kind. The journey only starts if the user remembers to open the app.
  • Timers stay silent when the phone is lockedA finished timer shows only inside the app, plus a VoiceOver announcement. If the app is in the background or the phone is locked, nothing alerts you. A 20-minute marinade can easily go too long.
  • The app doesn't know it's dinnertimeFor You doesn't use the time of day. A 90-minute braise and a 15-minute noodle dish rank the same at 7 pm. Cook time is on every card, so ranking by "ready by 7:30" would be cheap to add.
  • A stocked For You feed hasn't been screenshottedThese screenshots were taken with an empty pantry, so the "You have 8 of 9" reasons don't appear. Getting one means a new simulator capture once the Mac has memory free.
  • One coach answer is off-topicAsked "can I use apple cider vinegar here?", the coach led with a warning about doneness and food safety. This came from the test AI provider. Check it again on Gemini before the pilot.

Notifications

Today: none.Umma sends no notifications, local or push, and doesn't ask for notification permission. The PRD lists notifications as P2, and brief 015 left them out on purpose.
A

Timer alerts

Recommended first

When a cooking timer finishes, a local notification fires even if the phone is locked: Rest timer done: Gochujang Chicken Thighs, step 2.

What it takes
Small iOS-only PR. No server work or Apple push-notification keys. The app asks for notification permission the first time you start a timer, because that's the moment the reason is obvious.
Why
Fixes a real gap while cooking. Timers already count down to a fixed end time, so the alert time is exact.
B

Dinnertime reminder

Recommended next

Opt in, at a time you choose (6:30 pm by default): What's for dinner? See what fits your pantry. Tapping it opens For You.

What it takes
iOS only, using a repeating local notification and a toggle in Profile. Offer it after the first finished cook, not during onboarding.
Why
Keep the wording fixed. The phone can't recompute the pantry match at 6:30 without the server, so it shouldn't claim "you can make 3 things".
C

Personalised push

Defer

Messages like 3 recipes fit your pantry tonight or Mina Cho posted Kimchi Jjigae, sent from the server.

What it takes
Needs Apple push setup, a stored device token per user, a background worker and per-user scheduling. That's a backend PR series of its own.
Why
This is the most compelling version, but it's real infrastructure. The PRD lists notifications as P2, so it needs a logged decision either way.

Recommendation. Ship A as a small brief now. It closes a real cooking gap, and the permission request makes sense the first time a timer starts. Add B as an opt-in after the first finished cook. Keep C for later, when there's a reason to build push infrastructure.

Each of these brings notifications forward from P2, so each needs a DECISIONS entry.

Screens come from the onboarding smoke run (Explore, Following, creator page) and the cooking walkthrough capture (Pantry through Finish), both on 13 Nov 2026. The status-bar clocks show when each screen was captured, not the story's times.
